# @apodemakeles/dsh-macos-notify
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: when a conversation turn finishes while the harness window is not i
n the foreground, show a macOS system notification. It also leaves an in-app unread dot on sessions
that finished while you were away.
> Status: **v0.1.2**, distributed from GitHub. The unscoped npm name `dsh-macos-notify` belongs to a
nother package, so install this plugin from the `@apodemakeles` scope through GitHub.

## What it does
| turn/end reason | notification |

| `completed`, `max-tokens`, `blocked` | title = session name, body = completed (localized) |
| `err

or` | title = session name, body = failed (localized) |
| `aborted`, `interrupted`, unknown | silent

|
| subagent sessions | silent |

- Notifies only while the harness window is unfocused (`document.hasFocus() === false`).
- Clicking

a notification focuses the window and opens that session.
- A completion while the window is unfocus
ed also leaves a small unread dot on the session row, **even when the session stayed in the main vie
w**. The dot is green for success and red for failure; it clears when you click the row, start anoth
er run, or click the notification. When the official UI already shows its own background-completion

dot, this plugin does not add a second one.
- No history replay: the first projection value after st

artup or reconnect only seeds the baseline.
- **Settings → Notifications** has the master switch (de
fault on), permission state, and request-permission / test-notification buttons. The switch is store
d in the browser's localStorage.

## macOS notification permission
The first notification needs permission: click **Request permission** or **Send a test notification*
* in Settings → Notifications, then allow **DeepSeek Harness** in System Settings → Notifications.
A Focus mode can silently hold notifications (`delay delivery`) even when the app is allowed. Add De
epSeek Harness to that Focus mode's allowed apps, or turn the Focus mode off. The in-app unread dot
is independent of Focus.
## How it works
- **Host half** (`src/index.ts`, `src/projection.ts`) registers a `turn-notify` session projection.
It folds `turn/start` and `turn/end.reason` and exposes `{ turn, reason }` to the client. No webServ

er route, launch token, or Electron shell code.
- **Client half** (`src/client/index.ts`) watches th
e session list, detects a fresh projection turn, applies the master switch / subagent filter / reaso
n mapping / focus gate, shows a browser `Notification`, and opens the session with `uiWorkspace.open
Session(id)` on click. The unread dot is rendered through the official `sidebar.session.row.leading`

slot, only while the official status dot is idle.
- The host bundles `zod` for the projection schem

a; React stays external in the client and comes from the shell's module table.
- No network requests
: session names and turn reasons stay local.
## Compatibility
- DSH `0.2.x` (`engines.dsh`: `>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0`); tested with the desktop app `0.2.1-rc.2` and C

LI `0.2.0-rc.1`.
- macOS for notifications (browser/Electron Notification API); the unread dot is pl

atform-neutral.
- Node `>=22`.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`pnpm build` produces:

- `lib/index.js` — host ESM; registers the projection.
- `lib/client.js` — browser CJS bundle wrappe

d in the `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` factory.
- `lib/types/**` — declaration files.
For local development, install the checkout into a profile with `dsh plugin --profile web add link:$
(pwd)` (or the equivalent `pnpm --dir "$PROFILE" add link:$(pwd)` for the desktop profile).
